written.myAnswer: Hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂; empirical formula HO), glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆; empirical formula CH₂O), and benzene (C₆H₆; empirical formula CH).

Different compounds can have the same empirical formula because it gives only the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms. Different compounds can also have the same molecular formula if they are isomers, which have different structures. For example, glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) and ethanoic acid (C₂H₄O₂) both have empirical formula CH₂O.
Sand has a giant structure rather than discrete SiO₂ molecules. SiO₂ is its formula unit, showing the simplest whole-number ratio of silicon to oxygen atoms: 1:2.
